questions.q: What does the ternary operator x ? y : z do?
options: Acts as shorthand for an if-then-else statement, returning y if x is true and z otherwise
Declares a new variable of type x
Compares x and y for exact memory equality
Always returns z regardless of x
questions.explain: The ternary operator is shorthand for if-then-else statements: if x, a Boolean, is true, y is the result; otherwise z is the result.

questions.q: In Apex, what does the == operator check for sObjects, Strings, and most built-in types (not user-defined types)?
options: Reference equality only, exactly like Java
Value equality -- it compares the actual values, not memory references
Nothing -- == is not a legal operator in Apex
questions.explain: Unlike Java, == in Apex compares object value equality, not reference equality, except for user-defined types.

options: Whether x and y reference the exact same location in memory
Whether x is greater than or equal to y
It is identical to == in every case
questions.explain: === is the exact equality operator: if x and y reference the exact same location in memory, the expression evaluates to true.

questions.q: Given a && b || c, which operator is applied first?
options: || is always applied first regardless of position
They have equal precedence and apply strictly left to right
Apex requires parentheses here or it won't compile
questions.explain: Apex's operator table explicitly notes that && has precedence over ||, so a && b || c evaluates as (a && b) || c.

questions.q: What is the result of Integer a = 10 / 3; in Apex?
options: A compile error, since division always requires a Double
3, because dividing two Integers truncates the decimal portion
null, because division can't be assigned to an Integer
questions.explain: When x and y are both Integers, the division operator divides them and keeps an Integer result, truncating any remainder; using a Double on either side produces a Double result instead.
